threads.body: The nested `FunctionTool.call/acall` deduplication currently only short-circuits when `parent._workflow_agent_invocation` is set. If `call_tool` and the nested `FunctionTool` execution happen in different threads/tasks (so `_ACTIVE_WORKFLOW_TOOL` isn’t visible), standalone agent tool calls can regress to emitting duplicate `execute_tool` spans. The parent span being a `ToolInvocation` should be sufficient to dedupe in all cases.

When `AgentWorkflow` reaches `max_iterations` with `early_stopping_method="generate"`, LlamaIndex generates the successful final response later in `parse_agent_output`, so no subsequent step updates the member invocation and its `gen_ai.output.messages` remains the preceding tool-call response. threads.body: A failed handoff is still treated as a completed handoff here. Both the `ToolOutput.is_error` path and `prepare_to_drop_span` call this helper, so `_workflow_handoff` causes the member invocation to be stopped successfully and removed even though LlamaIndex only finalizes a handoff when `return_direct` is true **and** the tool output is not an error. If the workflow retries the current agent, telemetry is split into a second `invoke_agent` span; if the workflow aborts, the original agent span is incorrectly successful. Gate the pending-handoff close on a successful `ToolCallResult` and keep/appropriately fail the invocation on error.

threads.body: A mixed handoff/tool turn can incorrectly mark the handing-off agent successful. If the handoff finishes first, it stores `pending`; when a sibling tool later raises, `_finish_workflow_tool(..., handoff_succeeded=False)` still reaches this block, calls `_finish_member_agent(pending)` without the error, and removes the invocation. The subsequent workflow failure can no longer change that agent span to ERROR. Preserve the turn's first failure and pass it to `_finish_member_agent`, rather than tracking only whether the current completion was the handoff.
